auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We let $\overline{\mathbb R}$ denote the extended real line $\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ and write $\mathbb R_+$ for the positive half line $\{x\in\mathbb R:x>0\}$. Denote by $\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$ the set of all natural numbers and for any integer $t$, we let $[t]=\{1,2,...,t\}$.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The natural-number convention starts at one, so the k in Theorems 6/7 is positive. Extended-valued surrogate maximizers are allowed in (8), whereas F in (6) consists of real-valued functions.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
For any probability measure $P$ and measurable function $f$, we denote by $\|f\|_{P,k}$ the norm $\left(\int|f(x)|^k dP(x)\right)^{1/k}$. We will also denote this norm by $L_k(P)$. Also, $Pf$ will denote the integral $\int f dP$. For a concave function $f:\mathbb R^k\mapsto\overline{\mathbb R}$, the domain $\operatorname{dom}(f)$ will be defined as in (Hiriart-Urruty and Lemaréchal, 2004, p. 74), that is, $\operatorname{dom}(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R^k:f(x)>-\infty\}$. For $f:\mathbb R^2\mapsto\overline{\mathbb R}$, we denote by $f_{12}$ the partial derivative
\[
f_{12}(x,y)=\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial x\partial y}.
\]

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In what follows, similar to Zhao et al. (2015), we assume that the propensity scores, i.e. $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are known. This will hold in particular under a clinical trial like SMART (Kosorok and Laber, 2019), but not for observational data. When $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are unknown, they can be estimated using a logistic regression model. This additional estimation step will not change the approximation error but the estimation error will likely change.

unresolved_source_conventions.note: Remark 1 fixes optimal ties to +1, whereas the eta paragraph assigns -1 otherwise after the strict >1/2 case. Theorem 2 also uses set-valued surrogate rules yet writes a_1=dtilde_1(h_1) as a scalar equality. Set membership is not substituted for the printed equality.

The strict indicators yield no reward contribution when a score is zero. The following prose permits either action at zero, which need not match that formula for positive rewards. The original formula and tie claims are both preserved.

The source writes V_psi* through an extended-valued maximizer, then explicitly says Definition 1 does not require such maximizers to exist or be measurable. The corresponding supremum is recorded as the interpretation of the optimum; no attainment assumption is added to Fisher consistency.

The printed strict-concavity inequality quantifies all x,y in the effective domain without excluding x=y, making the literal inequality impossible at a repeated point. The original passage is saved, and the usual distinct-point restriction is not inserted into it.

The first branch is stated at h_1, but its failure conclusion uses capital H_1. The theorem does not specify how to choose a surrogate maximizer jointly across histories before stating all stagewise alternatives. The exact h_1/H_1 and scalar/set notation are retained.

The paper uses min(x-1,y-1,0), a figure caption max(x-1,y-1,0), and the Theorem 2 function min(x,y,1). The source’s shift discussion claims the two sides of (13) increase by C and 3C; substituting Y_1+C,Y_2+C instead leaves the contrast unchanged and adds 4C to the reward sum. These prose claims are not used to alter Theorem 2.

Condition 2 requires strict increase, positivity, reflected sum and limits, but does not require continuity or a derivative. Types A/B add differentiability away from zero. The theorem graphs keep these as separate requirements despite the source’s smoothed-loss terminology.

The final phrase says all t<t_0 without explicitly restricting t>0, although arbitrary positive real exponents are used. The intended small positive radius interpretation is recorded separately; the original t range is preserved. The exclusion of equality at the boundary permits atoms there.

The claimed equivalent contrast formulation drops absolute values and only controls positive small contrasts, whereas B controls both sides around one half. The saved theorem dependencies use B itself rather than this differing formula.

The condition literally bounds eta_1 and eta_2 away from zero. Decision boundaries occur at eta_t=1/2, so this does not imply the separation claimed in the surrounding prose and is not equivalent to an infinite noise exponent. Theorems 6/7 retain the literal source assumption without correction.

The later value display replaces fhat_t by phi(fhat_t) inside sign indicators. Under Condition 2 this always chooses positive actions, unlike the original value definition (5). The conflicting display is archived as A10; it is not substituted for the original definition.

Several sentences call V_psi(fhat) the psi-regret and V(fhat) the true regret, omitting the optimal-value subtraction. The original regret definitions and the actual theorem inequalities retain the subtraction. The informal wording does not redefine those quantities.

The informal class-approximation claim (20) omits scaling by a_n. Theorem 4 bounds scaled scores; Theorem 5 assumes explicitly that approximants in U_n divided by a_n are close to eta_t-1/2. No unstated scaling closure of U_n is added.

Theorem 5 does not explicitly impose the derivative-tail types A/B used in Theorem 4, while Condition 2 alone supplies no quantitative tail approach to its limits. The source scope is preserved with Condition 2 only; no proof-derived derivative condition is added to make the displayed rate easier to justify.

The source calls N the bracketing entropy but defines a number of brackets. Theorems 5/7 bound N, whereas (23) for Theorem 6 bounds log N with exponent 2rho_n. The metrics also differ; these conditions are not merged.

Bounds involving L2(P_n) depend on the observed sample. The main text does not state whether these inequalities are deterministic over all samples, almost sure, or on a specified event, nor an explicit epsilon range or uniformity of the implicit constants. These quantifier omissions are retained as unresolved.

The bracketing definition is for scalar functions, while (24) uses the pair class U_n with L2(P_n). The source does not specify a pair norm or identify the induced scalar loss class here. The formula is preserved without replacing U_n by its coordinate classes or a loss class.

Theorem 4 binds a_n tending to infinity but only calls delta_n a small number; it does not explicitly require delta_n to tend to zero. In Theorems 5-7 the probability guarantee is stated for each n,x, not as one event simultaneously covering all n,x. Uniformity of constants over varying rho_n, A_n and distributions is not fully specified.
